neighbours.label: a verb of setting off or moving away in a narrative ('after leaving', 'on the march', 'drove off', 'falling')
fire: Two weeks after leaving the harbor, the crew spotted land.
The soldiers were on the march before sunrise each day.
As the car pulled away from the curb, she waved goodbye.
Shortly after departing the station, the train broke down.
He was already walking away when they called his name.
After leaving office, the governor taught at a small college.
The herd was moving off toward the river at dusk.
As she was falling from the ladder, she grabbed the gutter.
quiet: Two weeks after reaching the harbor, the crew rested on land.
The soldiers were in their camp before sunrise each day.
As the car sat at the curb, she waved hello.
Shortly after arriving at the station, the train was cleaned.
He was already sitting down when they called his name.
While still in office, the governor taught at a small college.
The herd was resting near the river at dusk.
As she was standing on the ladder, she cleaned the gutter.

notes: Card: ' leaving' x2, ' march', Russian отъ|ез|жал, ' falling'; no dominant token. Logit effect promotes ' again', ' previously'. Near misses keep the narrative but use arriving or staying verbs.
